result.rationale: The newly added line in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`, gates on response.statusText, which is not guaranteed to be "OK" — notably it is often empty under HTTP/2 and in undici-based fetch implementations. A valid 200 token response could be rejected with a 400, breaking the Salesforce credential refresh flow that this diff introduces. This is a correctness defect in newly added code, though its manifestation depends on the runtime environment, so confidence is moderate.
